maths_errors.text: Both formulas follow the same triangle structure: the compound measure (D or P) is at the top — divide by it to isolate mass/volume or force/area.
maths_errors.correction: In the formula triangle, M (or F) goes at the top, with D and V (or P and A) on the bottom. You do not divide by D to find mass: M = D × V and F = P × A. Dividing only applies to volume and area: V = M ÷ D and A = F ÷ P.

maths_errors.text: Draw the D|MV triangle: D on top, M and V on the bottom. Cover the unknown to read off the formula.
maths_errors.correction: The triangle has M on top, with D and V on the bottom. With D on top, covering M would give D ÷ V, which is wrong; the correct result is M = D × V. This tip also contradicts commonMistakes[2], which correctly says 'Cover M → D × V'.

maths_errors.text: Same triangle pattern as density: P on top, F and A on the bottom.
maths_errors.correction: F goes on top, with P and A on the bottom. Covering F gives F = P × A; covering P gives P = F ÷ A; covering A gives A = F ÷ P.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: change freely between related standard units (eg time, length, area, volume/capacity, mass) and compound units (eg speed, rates of pay, prices) in numerical contexts
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson only says 'If units are mixed, convert first'. It never teaches how to convert, for example kg to g, m³ to cm³ (×1 000 000), cm² to m² (÷10 000), or g/cm³ to kg/m³ (×1000).

missing_spec_content.spec_text: compound units (eg density, pressure) in numerical and algebraic contexts
missing_spec_content.why: No algebraic context is taught, for example a density or pressure given as an expression, or forming and solving an equation from D = M/V.
The lesson never teaches comparing compound measures, for example deciding which material is denser or which arrangement gives the greater pressure.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: use compound units such as speed, rates of pay, unit pricing
missing_spec_content.why: The Basic foundation compound units in R11 (speed, rates of pay, unit pricing) are not taught. The lesson covers only density and pressure.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: use compound units such as density and pressure
missing_spec_content.why: Pressure is only stated as a formula. No pressure calculation is taught or worked, and no pressure units are used in any example.

cases_not_modelled.why: The only worked example is a density calculation. There is no pressure example.

cases_not_modelled.case: Rearranging to find mass or volume
cases_not_modelled.why: The worked example finds density directly. Finding M = D × V appears only as a check step, and V = M ÷ D is never worked.

cases_not_modelled.case: Rearranging to find force or area
cases_not_modelled.why: F = P × A and A = F ÷ P are stated but never worked.

cases_not_modelled.case: Unit conversion before or after calculating (e.g. cm² to m², g/cm³ to kg/m³)
cases_not_modelled.why: The worked example uses consistent units, so no conversion is shown.

cases_not_modelled.case: Comparison question (e.g. which of two objects is denser)
cases_not_modelled.why: The spec notes require comparisons, but no example compares two measures.
No example uses algebraic expressions for mass, volume, force or area.

cases_not_modelled.case: Multi-step density problem (e.g. combined mass or density of a mixture or alloy)
cases_not_modelled.why: This is a common exam style that needs mass = density × volume for each part followed by a total. It is not shown.

density.text: For density: D = M ÷ V (g/cm³ or kg/m³). Rearrange to find mass (M = D × V) or volume (V = M ÷ D). For pressure: P = F ÷ A (N/m² or N/cm²). Rearrange to find force (F = P × A) or area (A = F ÷ P). Both formulas follow the same triangle structure: the compound measure (D or P) is at the top — divide by it to isolate mass/volume or force/area. Units must be consistent throughout each calculation.
density.why: One paragraph carries two formulas, four rearrangements, two sets of units, the triangle method and a units rule. The triangle sentence is also confusing because it is wrong.

density.text: Cover M → D × V. Cover V → M ÷ D. Cover D → M ÷ V.
density.why: This is a chain of arrows that relies on a triangle the student never sees. It also conflicts with the triangle layout given in keyFacts.

density.text: Alternatively, write D = M/V and multiply both sides by V to get M = D × V.
density.why: Multiplying both sides by V first gives D × V = M. The step of then reading or swapping the sides is not stated.

density.text: Check by reversing: mass = density × volume = 2.7 × 50 = 135 g ✓.
density.why: The instruction holds the whole working and repeats it in the working field. It also uses M = D × V, a rearrangement the example never explains.

density.text: Pressure measures how much force acts on a given area — a stiletto heel exerts much higher pressure than a flat shoe of the same weight because the force is concentrated on a tiny area.
density.why: One sentence carries a definition, a comparison and a reason. 'A flat shoe of the same weight' is also misleading: the force comes from the wearer's weight, not the shoe's.

not_checked: No diagram of the formula triangle is supplied; only the text descriptions of the triangle could be checked.
